Method of Attack: Phishing email with ZIP attachment containing a shortcut file ('Company & Benefits.pdf.lnk') that executes a multi-stage PowerShell infection chain using ForFiles.exe to connect to C2 and download AES-encrypted payload
Heavy obfuscation in PowerShell scripts including reordering, IEX, byte value, compression, string replacement, backtick obfuscation
Anti-analysis checks (debugger detection, sandbox evasion via screen height and memory checks, system age check, language check)
Disabling network adapters and firewall blocking if checks fail, deleting drives and shutting down system
Disabling PowerShell Script Block Logging and adding Windows Defender exclusions
Persistence via Registry keys, scheduled tasks, Startup directory, and WMI subscriptions
Impacted Systems: Military contractors involved in weapon manufacturing including F-35 Lightning II fighter aircraft components supplier
Attack Vector: Phishing email with malicious ZIP attachment containing shortcut file
Indicators of Compromise: C2 domains: terma.wiki, terma.ink, terma.dev, terma.app, cobham-satcom.onrender.com
Use of ForFiles.exe command for execution
C2 infrastructure hosted initially on DigitalOcean then moved to Cloudflare
